0.note: Nice work getting through the mental model. One thing to sharpen from your written answer:

corrections.re: Why don't you need a step to "turn on" a tool in eve?
corrections.say: You wrote that the agent looks at its tools and picks one to use per message. That's true, but it's a different step. That's choosing a tool. The question was about turning one on. In eve you turn a tool on just by making the file in the tools/ folder. eve scans the folder and the file's name becomes the tool. No list to edit. So: making the file = on; the AI picking it per message = use. You described 'use.'

1.note: Good stuff. Your open answer nailed skills: on-demand, for long jobs you don't want on every call. The other half to hold onto: instructions.md is the opposite — short, always-on, for who it is and its hard rules. One heads-up: your quiz came through blank this time (submitted from the sidebar before hitting Check answers). No worries — you went 3/3 on it before.

replies.re: I'd like to run a /grill-me before we build the agent, to think through the strict guardrails.
replies.say: Yes — and it's saved. When we reach Module 5 (the first tool that changes real data) I'll raise the guardrails and start /grill-me myself. You don't have to remember it.

replies.re: What's the standard practice for how much instruction is enough while limiting tokens per call?
replies.say: Only put what's always true (identity, tone, hard rules), keep it to about one page, and push long or occasional how-tos into skills. Yours is ~350 words — right in the sweet spot. Shorter also means the model follows the rules more reliably.

2.note: 6 out of 6 on the harder quiz — excellent, including the cross-module one about a publish tool re-running. And your build-prep answer is exactly right: roster_overview needs no input, so its schema is z.object({}) — an empty shape, just like list_artists. You're ready to write it. Say "let's build" in the terminal and we'll do it together.

replies.re: Is listArtists() a real, written function, or just an idea the agent uses?
replies.say: Real, written code — not an idea. It lives in your database file, agent/lib/lonestar.ts. Open Browse the code → that file and search for export async function listArtists. You'll see the actual query that asks Supabase for every artist. The tool file just imports that function and calls it. So the chain is: tool → calls listArtists() → talks to the database → returns rows. The AI never writes that function; it only decides to call the tool that uses it.

replies.re: I don't see ctx in the code.
replies.say: Correct — it's not there, on purpose. execute can take a second argument: async execute(input, ctx) { ... }. That ctx is a toolbox eve would hand you (who's asking, a stop signal, the sandbox, etc.). Your three tools only need the input, so we left the second argument off entirely. It's optional — you add ctx only when a tool actually needs something from it. We'll likely use it later.
